idiom_name: trait View + presenter class (anonymous trait implementation as test double)
implementation_notes: Scala traits give the view contract without boilerplate, the presenter is a class taking the view trait and the model (both as constructor parameters), and a test double is an anonymous `new StationView { ... }` implementation or a stub class - nothing in the language replaces the classic structure, which is why the level is manual rather than idiomatic. Keep the view trait abstract and narrow so the concrete Swing/JavaFX class implements only what the presenter uses. Where the project has moved to reactive or Scala.js UI stacks, view/model synchronisation is handled declaratively by those frameworks (or by ScalaFX's JavaFX properties), and MVP earns its place mainly on the JVM with Swing/JavaFX or when one presenter must back several front ends.
pitfalls: A trait with concrete members that call abstract ones drags initialization-order pitfalls into the view contract; keep the trait abstract and let the concrete class define everything.
Immutable constructor parameters cannot be swapped for a test double after construction; create a fresh presenter per test (or take the view as a by-name/implicit parameter deliberately).
Overloads that erase to the same JVM signature (show(total: Double) and show(total: Int)) collide; give the view contract distinct method names.
